tasks.short: Plan training sessions with stores, prepare materials, train store staff in loss prevention, and record attendance.

steps.what: Loss prevention specialist plans training sessions with stores by e-mail
Store manager enrols their staff in the scheduled session in the learning system
Loss prevention specialist prepares training materials
Loss prevention specialist trains establishment personnel in loss prevention activities
Loss prevention specialist records attendance: on paper lists today; after the change by ticking who came on the enrolment list and adding walk-ins

tasks.design: Sessions are scheduled in the learning system ({LMS}), where store managers enrol their staff, instead of arranging dates by e-mail. Materials come from a shared library of loss prevention modules that the specialist adapts per store. The specialist ticks attendance on the enrolment list in the same system and adds walk-ins. Training staff in the store stays with the specialist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sessions were arranged by e-mail, materials remade and attendance kept on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Learning systems handle enrolment and attendance.
tasks.still_hard: Store staff turnover means constant retraining.
tasks.human_edge: Teaching a cashier how to refuse a suspicious refund politely.

evidence.claim: Learning systems can handle enrolment and attendance.

assumptions: Boundary: from the training need to attendance recorded; store procedures are outside.
Input contract: managers enrol staff; fallback is e-mail.
Training in the store does not change.

Managers enrol staff (s1e, share 1) in about the time an e-mail took; this is other-role time outside the specialist's savings. s1 keeps 40 for agreeing dates with stores; s2 keeps 60 because modules are adapted instead of written; s4 keeps 50 because names come from the enrolment and ticking who came stays.
research_questions: Is every new hire trained within a month?

incremental.description: Loss prevention specialist keeps the module library current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many managers keep arranging by e-mail and few modules fit a store without rewriting (10.3); high: enrolment and library used as designed (16.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Meet HR and risk management on cases and programs, share case information, track agreed actions, and prepare figures for meetings.

steps.what: Loss prevention specialist coordinates with risk management and human resources on investigations and programs
Loss prevention specialist shares case information with departments: by e-mail today; after the change by writing the update on the case in the register
Loss prevention specialist checks who needs to know: the HR or risk colleague, the case and which parts of it they may see
Loss prevention specialist grants the checked access on the case to the named colleague
Loss prevention specialist tracks agreed actions: in a spreadsheet today; after the change on the case's action list with owner and due date, and chases them
Loss prevention specialist prepares loss and incident figures for meetings

tasks.design: The specialist checks who needs to know and grants HR and risk management access to the cases they work on in the case register ({OPS_SYSTEM}), so case information is not sent by e-mail. Agreed actions are an action list on the case with owner and due date. A dashboard ({BI}) over the incident register gives figures for meetings. Coordinating with departments stays with the specialist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Case information travelled by e-mail and actions sat in a personal spreadsheet.
tasks.enabler_now: Case registers support role-based access and action lists.
tasks.still_hard: HR keeps its own files on the same staff.
tasks.human_edge: Agreeing with HR how to handle a long-serving employee caught stealing.

evidence.claim: Case registers can give role-based access and action lists.
The privacy code requires the least intrusive method and limits data to what is needed.

assumptions: Boundary: from the case or program to figures prepared; HR decisions are outside.
Input contract: access rights set per case; fallback is e-mail.

Coordination meetings and the access check and grant keep their full time. s2 keeps 50 because colleagues read the case and the specialist writes shorter updates; s3 keeps 70 because actions are entered once where owners see them and chasing stays; s4 keeps 40 because the dashboard gives the figures and choosing them stays.
research_questions: Do agreed actions close on time more often?

incremental.description: No ongoing upkeep: setting access per case is shown in s2c and s2g.

approvals.approved_version: Access to the parts of the case exactly as checked by the specialist in s2c, granted once to the named HR or risk colleague for this case; any wider access needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: departments still ask for e-mailed summaries and many incidents are outside the register (16.1); high: access and dashboard used as designed (25.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Analyse loss and incident data, compare equipment options with suppliers, decide recommendations, write the business case, check it, and send it to management.

steps.what: Loss prevention specialist analyses loss and incident data in spreadsheets
Loss prevention specialist compares equipment options with suppliers
Loss prevention specialist decides which processes or equipment to recommend to reduce risk exposure
Loss prevention specialist writes the business case
Loss prevention specialist checks the final business case: figures, options, recommendation and the management group it goes to
Loss prevention specialist sends the checked business case to management: by e-mail today, by sharing it in the document system after the change

tasks.design: A dashboard ({BI}) over stock losses and the incident register shows losses per store, cause and period, so the specialist does not build spreadsheets. The business case template pulls in the current loss figures for the stores concerned. Comparing options with suppliers and deciding what to recommend stay with the specialist. The specialist checks the final business case and its recipients and shares it with management in the document system.
tasks.previous_blocker: Loss data were compiled by hand for every proposal.
tasks.enabler_now: Dashboards over loss data and templates that pull figures.
tasks.still_hard: Savings from equipment are hard to prove in advance.
tasks.human_edge: Judging whether staff will actually use a new procedure.
tasks.altitude: The specialist argues the case instead of compiling figures.

evidence.claim: Veesion flags suspicious gestures in shop camera feeds and staff decide; the vendor claims up to 60% lower theft losses.
Shop cameras and loss analytics also watch staff; works council consent comes first.

assumptions: Boundary: from the risk review to the recommendation sent; purchasing is outside.
Input contract: loss and incident data in systems; fallback is spreadsheets.

Comparing options, deciding and checking keep their full time. s1 keeps 50 because the dashboard replaces building spreadsheets and the analysis stays; s4 keeps 70 because loss figures fill in and the specialist writes the case; sending keeps 20.
research_questions: Are more proposals approved with current figures?

incremental.description: Loss prevention specialist checks dashboard figures before use.

approvals.approved_version: The business case exactly as checked by the specialist in s5, shared once with the management group named there in the document system; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: much loss data sits outside the systems and each case needs new figures (14.7); high: data in the systems as designed (23.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan officers' shifts with the security firm, brief officers, supervise them on the floor, check their hours against invoices, and review performance with the firm.

steps.what: Loss prevention specialist prepares contract security officers' shifts with the security firm: by e-mail today, as a request in the firm's planning portal after the change
Loss prevention specialist checks the shift request before it goes: stores, dates, hours and number of officers
Loss prevention specialist submits the checked shift request in the firm's portal
Loss prevention specialist briefs officers on stores and risks
Loss prevention specialist directs the work of officers on the floor
Contract security officers record the hours they actually worked in the firm's portal
Loss prevention specialist checks officers' hours against the firm's invoices in a spreadsheet
Loss prevention specialist reviews service performance with the security firm

tasks.design: The specialist checks each shift request and submits it in the security firm's planning portal ({PARTNER_PORTAL}), where the firm confirms it, so shifts are not agreed by e-mail. Hours actually worked, recorded in the portal by the officers, are matched to the firm's invoice lines by code, and only differences are shown. Briefing, directing officers and reviewing performance stay with the specialist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Shifts were agreed by e-mail and hours checked against invoices by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Security firms run planning portals with hours registration.
tasks.still_hard: Last-minute changes still go by phone.
tasks.human_edge: Placing the right officer at a store with a known problem.

evidence.claim: Security firms can run planning portals with hours registration that match invoice lines.
Security organisations need a Justis licence and screened staff.

assumptions: Boundary: from store needs to performance reviewed; the contract is outside.
Input contract: the firm offers a portal; fallback is e-mail and spreadsheets.
Briefing and directing do not change.

The firm's planners' time does not change; officers' hour records (s4h) are other-role time. The shift check and submit keep their full time; s1 keeps 40 for agreeing changes; s4 keeps 30 for reading and resolving differences with the firm.

incremental.description: No ongoing upkeep: resolving hours differences with the firm is kept in s4.

approvals.approved_version: The shift request with stores, dates, hours and number of officers exactly as checked by the specialist in s1c, submitted once in the security firm's planning portal; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the firm uses the portal for only some stores, so e-mail and spreadsheet checks stay for the rest (9.5); high: all stores in the portal (17.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The loss prevention specialist keeps training staff, coordinating cases, recommending measures and directing officers; e-mail, spreadsheets and paper lists shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A specialist with more time in stores.
